data:
This course introduces the physical chemistry of biological systems. The topics include an introduction to the basics of statistical mechanics to understand the connections between macroscopic thermodynamic properties and microscopic molecular properties, chemical potentials, equilibrium states, binding cooperativity, behaviour of macromolecules in solution and at the interfaces, and solvation. We will
discuss protein structure, genomic analysis, single-molecule biomechanics, and biomaterials. To foster a deeper appreciation of the empirical aspects of the discipline, we will discuss Nuclear Magnetic Resonance measurements and provide practical demonstrations using the NMR spectrometer at Krea University. We will also discuss the recent developments in the use of Artificial Intelligence in
solving really hard Biophysics problems of understanding protein structure and dynamics. We will implement the computation of protein structure for practical sessions.
Associate Professor, Biological Sciences and Chemistry
